audits.mathematicalReason: Index intersections by east and south steps from A. Arrival probability starts at 1 at A and is propagated along outgoing streets: each available direction receives half at a choice, while a forced move receives the full probability. The recurrence gives P((3,2))=1/2 and P((2,3))=5/16. The former intersection has a forced southward move, whereas the latter splits equally. Thus P(C)=1/2+(1/2)(5/16)=21/32. State recursion is a valid assessed method, with addition and independence supplying the stated support; complete routes are not equally likely.

figureEvidence.fact: The map has three block columns and four block rows. A is the northwest corner, C is on the east boundary after three southward steps, and B is one further southward step below C. The compass identifies rightward as east and downward as south.

audits.mathematicalReason: Let x be the area of BDF. Since DC=2BD, the area of CDF is 2x, so CBF has area 3x. Because BE is a median, A and C have equal perpendicular distances from BE; hence ABF also has area 3x. Therefore ABD has area 4x, ABC has area 12x, and BCE has area 6x. Subtracting BDF leaves FDCE with area 5x, giving the requested ratio 1/5. The alternative route is also valid: if T is the midpoint of DC, then ET is parallel to AD, and BD=DT makes D the midpoint of BT. Parallel-line proportionality in BET then makes F the midpoint of BE. The 72° angle is unnecessary.

figureEvidence.fact: D lies on BC, E lies on AC, and AD and BE meet at the interior point F. Triangle BCE is partitioned into triangle BDF and quadrilateral FDCE.

audits.mathematicalReason: Let the common side length be s. Regularity makes OP=1 the common apothem, so the five center-based triangles give pentagon area 5s/2. The vertex-based triangles ABC, ACD, and ADE instead give area s(AQ+AP+AR)/2; perpendicular feet on extended sides remain valid heights. Consequently AQ+AP+AR=5. The symmetry axis through A and the midpoint P of CD contains O, with AP=AO+OP=AO+1. Thus AO+AQ+AR=4. Regular-polygon geometry and the listed area-decomposition route are defensible scopes.

audits.mathematicalReason: Set d=AD/AB, and provisionally place E on AC. If h and k are the perpendicular heights of C and E above AB, right triangles give AB=(1+√3)h and AD=(1+1/√3)k. Hence k/h=√3d, and the area ratio ADE/ABC is √3d². Equal areas require √3d²=1/2, whose positive solution is d=1/12^(1/4). This location is valid: the cut through C has d=1/√3, and the computed d is smaller. If E were on CB, the piece containing A would already have area fraction at least 1/√3>1/2. The sine-law route independently gives AE/AC=√3d, using angles 75° and 105° and sin(105°)=sin(75°), so both listed routes are valid.

audits.mathematicalReason: Routes beginning M→A have two continuations: A→C→N and A→D→C→N. Routes beginning M→B either continue directly to N, continue through C, or continue through A and then take one of those two continuations, giving 1+1+2=4. The first-edge cases are disjoint, so the total is 2+4=6. This directly supports the addition-principle mapping without requiring a more elaborate graph or recursion scope.

figureEvidence.fact: The directed edges are M→A, M→B, B→A, A→D, A→C, B→C, B→N, D→C, and C→N. In particular, the horizontal connection between A and B points toward A, not toward B.

audits.mathematicalReason: The stair-step construction gives row n a total of 2n−1 squares. Alternation beginning and ending unshaded makes n of them unshaded and n−1 shaded. Thus row 37 contains 37−1=36 shaded squares. Expressing and evaluating the figure pattern is exactly the proposed scope.

figureEvidence.fact: The four displayed rows contain 1, 3, 5, and 7 squares, with 0, 1, 2, and 3 shaded squares. Every displayed row alternates shading and has unshaded squares at both ends.

audits.mathematicalReason: The inscribed angle at A gives arc BC=60°. Equal chords AB and AC then give minor arcs AB=AC=150°, and arc AD=120°. If x is arc AG, equality DG=AB permits x=30° or 90°; the condition BG>GA selects x=30°, with BG=120°. Consequently arc GBC=180°, so GC is a diameter. Angles GAF and AGF are both 60°, making AFG equilateral and AF=AG. Triangle AGE is right at A with angle G=60°, so AE=√3 AG. In right triangle AGC, angle C=15°, hence AG/AC=tan(15°)=2−√3. Using the common angle at A, the area ratio is (AF/AB)(AE/AC)=√3(2−√3)²=7√3−12. This validates the cyclic-angle/right-triangle route; the same arc configuration also supports unit-circle coordinates and linear intersections. Similarity of AFE and ABC is not assumed.

figureEvidence.fact: The cyclic order is A, G, B, C, D. Along chord DG the points occur in the order D, E, F, G, with E on AC and F on AB. These incidences determine which rays and intercepted arcs are used in the angle calculations.
